newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed sees Fermi nuke on line Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed sees Fermi nuke on line Tuesday.

text.p: Detroit Edison, operator of the 1,116 megawatt (MW) Fermi 2 nuclear power plant, said Tuesday it expected to have the unit back on line later today, reaching full power production sometime next week.
"We are going to try to phase it back on line later today and should hit full power next week," a company spokesman said.
Detroit Edison was forced to interrupt restart operations Monday when they ran into problems with a new turbine, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Tuesday.
According to the NRC's daily status report, the unit was operating at 50 percent of its rated capacity when the turbine went off balance.
Production was then dropped back to 18 percent. It was not, however, contributing power to the grid at that time.
Detroit Edison, which owns and operates the Fermi facility, is a subsidiary of DTE Energy Corp.
